action.description: Root analysis node only; no implementation attached.
action.rationale: Establish problem model before selecting the first implementation path.
action.title: World-model root

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel XPU/Triton path should favor dense fp16 dot work with static C=32, N=16, hidden=128; XMX-friendly matmul shapes may matter, but very small K/N shapes risk underutilization.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The block is mostly many small dense linear projections plus small-window attention; total arithmetic is dominated by qkv/proj/MLP rather than the 16x16 attention softmax.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Small per-token channel dimension and fragmented windows may fail to saturate compute unless batched/tilized across many tokens/windows.

memory_bandwidth.notes: NHWC input/output are dense and contiguous by channel; window attention loads are strided across rows but small. Weights are tiny and highly reusable. Eager reference likely pays launch/layout overhead and intermediate traffic for LN, qkv, attention, proj, LN, fc1, GELU, fc2.
memory_bandwidth.risk: A custom kernel that materializes large intermediates or rereads x repeatedly may become bandwidth/latency limited despite small weights.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window attention can hold 16x32 q/k/v fragments and 16x16 scores/softmax in registers if mapped carefully; full MLP hidden=128 per token is larger and may need tiling over hidden dimension.
register_pressure.risk: Over-fusing attention, projection, two LNs, and MLP in one kernel could exceed registers and reduce occupancy on Intel XPU.

nodes.notes:
1) Classification: mixed dense linear algebra + normalization reductions + small-window attention/softmax + elementwise residual/GELU. Primary output is y[B,H,W,C] = fp16 tensor same shape as input. Reductions: LayerNorm over C=32, q/k/v and projection reductions over C=32, attention reductions over N=16, MLP reductions over C=32 and hidden=128. Access is mostly dense NHWC; window partition introduces regular strided loads, not sparse indirect.
2) Canonical math: for each pixel token t, z1=LN32(x_t); for each 4x4 window w, Q,K,V=z1_w @ Wqkv^T + b, A=softmax(QK^T/sqrt(32)+RPE[16,16]), a=A V, p=a @ Wproj^T + bproj, r1=x+p. Then z2=LN32(r1); h=GELU(z2 @ Wfc1^T + b1); m=h @ Wfc2^T + b2; y=r1+m. Windows and tokens are independent except within each 4x4 attention window; online stable softmax possible over N=16 but full score matrix is small.
3) Layout/access: input/output [1,720,1280,32] fp16 contiguous NHWC, 921600 tokens. Windows: nH=180,nW=320,Bw=57600,N=16,C=32. Weights: qkv [96,32], proj [32,32], fc1 [128,32], fc2 [32,128], biases fp16, rpe [1,1,16,16]. Dominant reads/writes are intermediate activations if not fused; weights fit cache/constant-like reuse. Per-window rows have stride 1280*32 elements; intra-pixel channels contiguous.
4) Bottleneck hypotheses: Regime A eager/torch baseline is launch and intermediate-memory dominated because many small ops over huge token count. Regime B custom attention-only is latency/register dominated by small N=16 softmax and strided window loads; qkv/proj still significant. Regime C MLP-heavy path is compute dominated by two dense projections per token, but small K=32/128 may be shape-efficiency limited. Regime D full fusion may become register/occupancy limited but minimizes memory traffic.
5) Design knobs: parallelize by window, by token tile, or hybrid; tile token rows and output channels; decide whether to materialize r1 and/or fc1 hidden; fp32 vs fp16 accumulation for LN/softmax/dots; exact GELU via erf vs approximation; specialize constants B=1,H=720,W=1280,C=32,N=16,hidden=128; exploit tiny reusable weights; choose number of Triton kernels vs fusion level.
6) Skeleton: phase LN1 per token with fp32 mean/var, phase window qkv + attention + proj + residual, phase LN2 per token, phase fc1 + GELU + fc2 + residual. Registers hold C=32 vectors, LN stats, attention row scores/probabilities, small output fragments; shared/local staging may help q/k/v per window; synchronization only within a program instance if multiple lanes cooperate on one window/tile.
7) Candidate families: full block spatial fusion for minimum traffic but high register risk; attention-centered window path for localized replacement of PyTorch's most layout-fragmented part; MLP/LN-centered token path for the largest arithmetic share with regular dense access.

action.description: Implement a fixed-shape custom Triton path for the whole forward using a small number of kernels: one window-attention/residual stage and one token-MLP/residual stage, with LayerNorm fused into the consuming stage where practical.
action.rationale: The reference creates many large intermediates and launches many framework kernels. Specializing to B=1,H=720,W=1280,C=32,window=4x4,hidden=128 can remove layout reshapes, reduce memory traffic, and exploit tiny fixed reductions.
action.title: Build specialized full-block Triton forward

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Best chance to batch enough independent windows/tokens for Intel XPU occupancy; fixed fp16 dot shapes C=32/N=16/hidden=128 can be tuned for XMX or SIMD lowering.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Covers all arithmetic in the block, including the dominant linear layers and attention. Static dimensions allow aggressive specialization.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: If Triton lowering for the chosen small dot shapes is poor, the custom path may lose to optimized PyTorch linear kernels.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Potentially minimizes global activation traffic by avoiding qkv/attn/fc1 materialization or at least limiting materialization to r1 between phases.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If implementation must spill q/k/v, attention, or hidden activations, much of the intended bandwidth advantage disappears.

register_pressure.notes: Attention per window and MLP hidden tiles both require many live values; likely needs decomposition into at least two kernels or hidden-channel tiling.
register_pressure.risk: Register spill and low occupancy are the primary failure modes for this family.

nodes.notes:
SELF_CHECK: This sibling is an end-to-end replacement plan; it cannot be combined as the same first iteration with attention-only or MLP-only focus because it allocates the iteration budget to integration and global scheduling rather than isolating one subsystem.
Plan emphasis: specialize all constants and preserve reference order/numerics closely, especially fp32 LayerNorm reductions and stable softmax.

action.description: Implement only the W-MSA region in Triton: consume norm1 output or fuse LN1, compute qkv, 16x16 softmax with RPE, projection, window reverse, and first residual; leave norm2 and MLP initially in PyTorch modules.
action.rationale: The attention path has awkward 4x4 window partitioning and several small operations where eager PyTorch overhead and intermediate traffic are likely high. Replacing it first gives a correctness-focused, localized kernel target.
action.title: Accelerate the window-attention subgraph first

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Each window has N=16,C=32 and there are 57600 independent windows; parallelism is abundant but per-window work is small.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Targets qkv/proj and attention. The small score matrix fits in registers, and RPE is tiny.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Per-window programs may be too fine-grained, causing scheduling overhead and underutilized vector units unless grouped over multiple windows.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Can remove qkv, attention-score, and window-partition intermediates; however MLP intermediates remain in PyTorch.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If LN1 is not fused, reading/writing norm1 output may limit the speedup.

register_pressure.notes: 16x16 score/probabilities plus q/k/v fragments are manageable compared with full-block fusion.
register_pressure.risk: Holding all q/k/v for a window while also computing projection may still cause spills depending on program mapping.

nodes.notes:
SELF_CHECK: This sibling is mutually exclusive as a first target with full-block or MLP-first plans because it keeps the second half of the block unchanged to isolate attention/window-layout benefits.
Plan emphasis: validate window indexing, RPE dtype/layout, stable softmax, and residual placement before adding MLP fusion.

action.description: Implement the post-attention token MLP region in Triton: norm2 over C=32, fc1 to hidden=128, exact GELU, fc2 back to C=32, and final residual; initially call the reference attention path unchanged.
action.rationale: The MLP has the largest regular dense arithmetic share per token and avoids window-strided indexing. It is a lower-risk first kernel that can beat eager chains by fusing LayerNorm, GELU, and residual around the dense projections.
action.title: Accelerate the token MLP subgraph first

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Regular NHWC token stream with 921600 independent rows; dense fp16 projections with K=32 and hidden=128 are more regular than attention windows.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Targets the dominant MLP math and should map cleanly to tiled dot operations over token blocks and hidden/output channels.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: PyTorch linear for large flattened [921600,32] x [32,128] may already be efficient, so fusion must compensate for any custom matmul inefficiency.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Can avoid materializing norm2 and GELU/fc1 hidden if fc2 accumulation is streamed or tiled; otherwise still saves at least some elementwise traffic.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Materializing hidden [921600,128] would be very expensive and may erase gains.

register_pressure.notes: LN state is tiny; the hidden=128 expansion is the main register/tile pressure and should be handled in chunks.
register_pressure.risk: Streaming fc2 through GELU values increases live accumulators and may require careful tiling to avoid spills.

nodes.notes:
SELF_CHECK: This sibling is a first-target alternative to attention/full-block work because it deliberately avoids window attention complexity and spends the iteration on the regular dense MLP path.
Plan emphasis: exact GELU compatibility, fp32 LayerNorm statistics, and avoiding a large hidden activation write are the key correctness/performance constraints.

kernel_summary: This is a fixed-shape simplified Swin block on NHWC fp16 input [1,720,1280,32] with 57600 independent 4x4 windows, single-head attention N=16,C=32, and an MLP hidden size 128. The computation is mixed: fp32 LayerNorm reductions over 32 channels, dense qkv/proj/fc projections, a tiny stable softmax over 16 keys with RPE, exact GELU, and residual adds. The main optimization opportunity is reducing framework launch/layout/intermediate overhead while preserving reference numerics; dense weights are small and highly reusable, but custom Triton must avoid register spills and poor small-matmul utilization on Intel XPU.
open_questions: What correctness tolerance is used by the evaluator for fp16 outputs, especially for LayerNorm accumulation, softmax, and GELU exactness?
Does Triton on Intel XPU generate efficient fp16 dot/XMX code for small K shapes such as 32 and 128, or should kernels favor scalar/vector reductions?
Is using some PyTorch modules inside ModelNew allowed for an initial hybrid solution, or must every major operation be custom Triton?
What is the actual baseline latency split among LayerNorm, qkv/proj, attention softmax, fc1/fc2, GELU, and reshape/permute overhead on Arc Pro B70?
Are model weights guaranteed contiguous fp16 with the same layout as nn.Linear weight [out,in], and is rpe_bias always pre-gathered contiguous fp16?
How does the Intel XPU backend handle tl.erf or exact GELU performance and accuracy compared with torch.nn.GELU default approximate='none'?
What launch overhead and occupancy behavior should be expected for many independent small-window Triton programs on this device?
